key_insight: ReLMem learns a fixed-size recurrent patient memory that updates visit by visit, preserving useful history for longitudinal EHR prediction without reprocessing the full record.
clinical_relevance: This could make large-model EHR workflows much more efficient for tasks like medication prediction by lowering storage and compute demands while keeping performance close to full-history modeling.
method: Adds lightweight compression adapters to a frozen LLM to update memory from the previous state plus each new visit.
Uses multi-granularity training to align compressed-memory attention with full-history attention under the same queries.
Adds final-step prediction supervision so the learned memory supports downstream cross-entropy prediction.
evidence_signal: In EHR medication prediction, ReLMem nearly matched the full-history baseline while reducing retained historical storage by 97.1%, and beat the strongest compressed-memory baseline by 4.66 macro-F1 and 4.75 micro-F1.
watch_item: Results are shown on one EHR prediction task, so broader clinical validation and careful monitoring of information loss under fixed memory budgets are still needed.
paper_title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling
